sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Baal Shem Tov's interpretation of the verse "Blow in the month a shofar," that the word "in the month" modifies the blowing, indicating that each year the shofar blasts must be in a new manner, because a new aspect of the shofar is renewed each year, and this is effected by Israel's service.

translations.translation: And with this we explain what is written,
"Blow in the month a shofar,"
for the precise point of the Baal Shem Tov on this is known,
that seemingly it should have said "Blow a shofar in the month,"
and he explains regarding this,
that what is written "Blow in the month"
("in the month" adjacent to "blow")
is,
that "in the month" refers to "blow,"
that each year the blasts must be in a new manner.
And the reason for this,
is that each year the aspect of the shofar is renewed.
And since all the matters above are brought about by the service of the Children of Israel,
according to the teaching of the Maggid
in his explanation of the Mishnah,
"Know what is above from you," that everything that is above, all of it is from you,
therefore the shofar blowing of Israel must be in a new manner, so that through this a new matter will be effected above.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that just as the shofar blowing on Rosh HaShanah is renewed each year, so too all mitzvos must be seen as new, and the renewal in the shofar—which is the root of the year—draws renewal into all mitzvos throughout the year by renewing G-d's kingship.

translations.translation: And now, just as it is with the mitzvah of shofar blowing on Rosh HaShanah, that each year it is in a new manner,
so too is it with all the mitzvos,
as our sages said,
"Each day they should be in your eyes like new,"
and even more so, actually new.
However, with shofar blowing,
since it is a mitzvah that encompasses the entire year,
as is known
the reason why it is called "Rosh HaShanah" (Head of the Year)
(and not "Beginning of the Year"),
because it is the head that includes all the days of the year,
this matter is to a greater degree.
And it can be said,
that this matter
(the renewal in shofar blowing)
is the root from which it is drawn that also the mitzvos of the entire year will be new.
For the mitzvah of shofar blowing on Rosh HaShanah, its matter is "that you coronate Me over you,"
and since the manner of the mitzvos is according to the manner of "you coronate Me over you,"
as is understood from our sages' statement,
"Accept My kingship first, and then I will decree decrees upon you,"
therefore, through the shofar blowing being in a new manner, so it is done in all the mitzvos.
For through "Blow in the month," renewal is brought about, as it were, in the attribute of His kingship,
in that He reigns over Israel
("you coronate Me over you"),
and through this also in His kingship over all the worlds
[for this too is done by and for Israel,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills Israel's request, "Reign over the entire world in Your glory,"
that in this
("the entire world")
are included all the worlds entirely],
that on each Rosh HaShanah new life is drawn into the entire order of the chain of descent,
new life that never yet existed,
as the Alter Rebbe wrote in Iggeres HaKodesh,
and this life is then drawn also throughout all the days of the year,
through the twelve heads of months,
as is explained at length in the book Atteres Rosh of the Mitteler Rebbe.
And so too is it with the mitzvos,
that the matter of renewal in the mitzvos
("each day etc. new")
throughout the entire year,
is drawn from the renewal of shofar blowing on Rosh HaShanah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains why when Rosh HaShanah falls on Shabbat the shofar is not blown in the provinces, because on Shabbat the aspect of delight (shofar) is already present in perfection without human labor, unlike on a weekday when it must be effected by Israel's blowing.

translations.translation: And with this will be understood
that on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat, they do not blow in the provinces,
because what is needed in blowing the shofar on Rosh HaShanah is
(as above)
in order to effect through this the shofar above,
and on Shabbat this aspect
(shofar)
exists without the labor of man.
For it is known,
that on a Festival we say "Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons," that Israel sanctified the seasons,
but Shabbat is sanctified and stands,
and is not dependent on Israel to sanctify it.
Therefore on Shabbat there are many matters that are prepared,
and some of them are in a manner of perfection,
even without the labor of man.
And it is written,
"to make the Shabbat,"
that Israel make the Shabbat,
and so it is written,
"Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it,"
that Israel need to sanctify the Shabbat.
And the matter is,
that on Shabbat there are two levels,
that Shabbat is sanctified and stands of itself,
and that which Israel add to it through their service.
For Shabbat is the matter of delight,
and nevertheless they said,
"Whoever delights in the Shabbat,"
that they need to delight in the Shabbat,
and so it is written,
"And you shall call the Shabbat a delight,"
that one must call and draw delight into Shabbat,
for through the service of Israel they draw into Shabbat a more elevated delight.
But there is a delight on Shabbat of itself,
from the aspect that Shabbat is sanctified and stands,
and it is a delight in perfection.
For the entirety of the matter of Shabbat is that then perfection is made in all of creation,
as it is written,
"And the heavens and the earth and all their host were completed,"
that "were completed" is the matter of perfection, according to the explanation of the Tzemach Tzedek,
from which it is understood that also the delight of Shabbat
(as it is of itself)
is in perfection.
And this is why on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat there is not so much necessity to blow the shofar in the provinces.
For the shofar is an aspect of delight,
and as is explained in the maamar,
that "shofar" is from the term "improve your deeds"
and from the term "He who gives words of beauty"
(and also other expressions brought in the maamar there),
whose matter is delight.
And since everything that is above, all of it is from you,
therefore in order that there be the aspect of delight
(shofar)
above,
this is done through the shofar blowing of Israel.
For all this is on Rosh HaShanah that falls on a weekday.
But on Shabbat,
the matter of delight is prepared
(without the labor of man),
to the extent that the delight is in perfection
(as above),
therefore on Rosh HaShanah that falls on Shabbat, the mitzvah of shofar blowing is not in such force
(with all the fuss)
as on Rosh HaShanah that falls on a weekday,
and therefore it is deferred due to the concern that one might carry it etc.
